answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity linearly expensive. Every agent that wants to transact must lock a collateral bond, returned only after it builds real transaction history and slashed if peers flag duplicate accounts. Because the deposit scales with the number of identities, an attacker wanting a thousand fake voters on the terrace must lock a thousand bonds, so each extra identity costs real copper up front while an honest agent pays once. A falcon audit then compares on-chain activity graphs to catch clusters sharing one funding source.
